**`mermaid.initialize()` called on every render** `mermaid.initialize()` is invoked at the top level of `MermaidContent` — a side effect during render. With `reactStrictMode: true` (set in `next.config.mjs`), React intentionally renders components twice in development to surface side effects, so `initialize()` will fire multiple times per mount. When multiple diagrams appear on the same page, each instance also resets the global mermaid config. Move the initialization into a `useEffect` so it only runs once per theme change: ``` useEffect(() => { mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'loose', fontFamily: 'inherit', themeCSS: 'margin: 1.5rem auto 0;', theme: resolvedTheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'default', }); }, [resolvedTheme, mermaid]); ```
Prompt To Fix With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: searchfn/docs/components/mdx/mermaid.tsx Line: 31-38 Comment: **`mermaid.initialize()` called on every render** `mermaid.initialize()` is invoked at the top level of `MermaidContent` — a side effect during render. With `reactStrictMode: true` (set in `next.config.mjs`), React intentionally renders components twice in development to surface side effects, so `initialize()` will fire multiple times per mount. When multiple diagrams appear on the same page, each instance also resets the global mermaid config. Move the initialization into a `useEffect` so it only runs once per theme change: ``` useEffect(() => { mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: false, securityLevel: 'loose', fontFamily: 'inherit', themeCSS: 'margin: 1.5rem auto 0;', theme: resolvedTheme === 'dark' ? 'dark' : 'default', }); }, [resolvedTheme, mermaid]); ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````

**Cached render reuses a stale mermaid element ID** `mermaid.render(id, chart)` embeds the component's unique `id` (from `useId()`) as a CSS/HTML ID inside the generated SVG. The render result is then cached under `${chart}-${resolvedTheme}`. When a second component instance renders the same chart+theme combination (e.g., the same diagram appears on two different pages and the user navigates between them without a full reload, or the same chart is used twice on one page), it receives the **cached SVG that contains the first instance's `id` string**. If both instances exist in the DOM simultaneously, their injected SVGs will have **duplicate element IDs**, which is invalid HTML and can break `bindFunctions` (which queries by ID to attach event handlers). A minimal fix is to include `id` in the cache key so each component instance always generates its own SVG: ```suggestion const { svg, bindFunctions } = use( cachePromise(`${id}-${chart}-${resolvedTheme}`, () => { return mermaid.render(id, chart.replaceAll('\\n', '\n')); }), ); ``` This trades some memory for correctness; the module-level cache would then be unbounded, so consider limiting it or scoping the cache to the component instance (e.g., `useRef`) rather than module level.

**`as any` cast hides API shape mismatch** `(fumadocsSource as any).files()` suppresses type checking for what could be a real API shape difference between the fumadocs version in use and the expected interface. If `fumadocsSource` changes its shape in a future fumadocs upgrade, this will silently break at runtime with a method-not-found error. If the types between `fumadocs-mdx` and `fumadocs-core` are misaligned, consider explicitly casting to the narrowest known type or filing an issue upstream. At minimum, a comment explaining why `as any` is needed here would help future maintainers.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Build docs-theme before running SearchFn docs build**

The `prebuild` script runs `fumadocs-mdx` but never builds `@superfunctions/docs-theme`, even though this app imports that package and its published exports point to `dist/*`. On a clean checkout where `packages/docs-theme/dist` is not present, `next build` cannot resolve theme exports (for example `DocsRootLayout`), so the docs package build fails until the theme package is built first.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include instance id in Mermaid render cache key**

Caching rendered Mermaid output by only `${chart}-${resolvedTheme}` reuses one SVG across component instances with identical chart text. Since `mermaid.render` embeds the per-instance `useId()` into generated SVG IDs, this produces duplicate IDs in the DOM and can break bindings/interactivity when the same diagram appears multiple times on a page.

`What Mermaid securityLevel options are available and what are the security implications?`

💡 Result:

The Mermaid securityLevel configuration option controls the level of trust for parsed diagrams, affecting how HTML tags in text and interactive features like click handlers are handled. The available options are: - "strict" (default): HTML tags in the text are encoded (e.g., < becomes <), and click functionality is disabled. This provides the highest security by preventing XSS via malicious HTML or JavaScript in diagrams. - "loose": HTML tags in text are allowed, and click functionality is enabled. This increases risk of XSS if untrusted diagram sources are rendered, as attackers could inject HTML/JS via click directives. - "antiscript": HTML tags in text are allowed (but script elements are removed), and click functionality is enabled. Slightly safer than "loose" by blocking <script> tags, but still vulnerable to other JS via event handlers. - "sandbox": All rendering occurs in a sandboxed iframe, preventing any JavaScript from running in the parent context. This blocks XSS but may disable interactive features like popups, links to other tabs, or sequence diagram scripts. Security implications: Lower security levels ("loose", "antiscript") enable HTML rendering and interactions, allowing stored/reflected XSS if diagrams from untrusted sources (e.g., user input) are rendered—exploitable via click callbacks executing JS or CSS exfiltration. Use "strict" or "sandbox" for untrusted content; "loose"/"antiscript" only for trusted diagrams (e.g., static site generators). Default "strict" balances security and functionality. Additionally, configure DomPurify for extra sanitization, and keep Mermaid updated for patches (e.g., CVE-2022-31108).

Citations:

- 1: https://mermaid.js.org/config/schema-docs/config-properties-securitylevel.html
- 2: https://mermaid.js.org/config/schema-docs/config.html
- 3: https://github.com/OneUptime/oneuptime/security/advisories/GHSA-wvh5-6vjm-23qh

**Move `mermaid.initialize()` call outside of component render path.**

The `mermaid.initialize()` configuration is called on every `MermaidContent` render. Since initialization is idempotent and configuration doesn't change per-render, move this to a `useEffect` or a module-level initialization to avoid unnecessary reinitialization overhead.

Regarding `securityLevel: 'loose'`: This is appropriate here because (1) chart content originates from MDX files (author-controlled, not user input), and (2) the component uses `bindFunctions` to enable interactive Mermaid features (click handlers, links) which require loose mode. Stricter security levels would disable these features.

`For the current versions of fumadocs-mdx and fumadocs-core, what is the typed return shape of `docs.toFumadocsSource()`, and what is the recommended typed way to pass its files into `loader({ source: ... })` without using `any`?`

💡 Result:

Current versions: fumadocs-mdx v14.2.11 (published 2026-03-19), fumadocs-core v16.7.6 (published 2026-03-25). The typed return shape of docs.toFumadocsSource is Source<{ metaData: ..., pageData: ... }> (generic Source from fumadocs-core/source, with custom metaData and pageData types inferred from the content collections defined in source.config.ts via defineDocs). The recommended typed way to pass it into loader({ source: ... }) without any is: ts import { loader } from 'fumadocs-core/source'; import { docs } from './.source'; // generated types export const source = loader({ source: docs.toFumadocsSource, baseUrl: '/docs', }); To get full type inference for the resulting source (e.g., for InferPageType<typeof source>), import from the generated .source directory after running fumadocs-mdx (or in postinstall). This provides type-safe access to source.getPage, etc. The generic allows custom typing for page and meta data without any. For custom typing the loader result: ts import type { InferPageType, InferMetaType } from 'fumadocs-core/source'; export type DocsPage = InferPageType<typeof source>; export type DocsMeta = InferMetaType<typeof source>; This is the official pattern shown in docs and examples.

🌐 Web query:

`fumadocs-core Source type .files() method documentation`

💡 Result:

In fumadocs-core, the Source type (from fumadocs-core/source) is an interface used for custom content sources passed to the loader function. It includes a files property, which is an array of file objects representing pages and metadata. Example from official docs: ts import { Source } from 'fumadocs-core/source'; export function createMySource: Source<{ /* custom types */ }> { return { files: [ { type: 'page', path: 'folder/index.mdx', data: { title: 'Hello World', // ... }, }, { type: 'meta', path: 'meta.json', data: { title: 'Docs' /* ... */ }, }, ], }; } Each file object has: - type: 'page' or 'meta' - path: Virtual path (e.g., 'folder/index.mdx') - data: Content/frontmatter data No .files method exists on the loaded source object; files is a static array in the input Source. The loaded source exposes methods like getPage, getPages, getPageTree. Virtual file storage is accessible via loader plugins' transformStorage({ storage }), where storage.files is a Map-like object with get, set, read etc. Official documentation: https://www.fumadocs.dev/docs/headless/source-api/source

💡 Result:

In fumadocs-mdx, defineDocs returns an object with docs (doc collection) and meta (meta collection) properties. These collections have a files option in their configuration, which is string[] | undefined (glob patterns to include/exclude files; all files included if unspecified). toFumadocsSource is a method on collections returned by defineCollections or defineDocs (e.g., docs.toFumadocsSource), converting the collection to a Source object compatible with fumadocs-core's loader (as in multiple({ docs: docs.toFumadocsSource })). **Use the proper fumadocs-mdx pattern for source wiring.**

Line 9 uses `(fumadocsSource as any).files()` which is structurally incorrect. In fumadocs-mdx, `docs.toFumadocsSource()` returns a `Source` object where `files` is a property (array), not a method. 

Use the official pattern instead:

```typescript
export const source = loader({
  baseUrl: "/docs",
  source: docs.toFumadocsSource,
});
```

Pass the function directly to `loader`—don't call it first. This provides full type safety and eliminates the need for `any` casts. If you need to extract files for other reasons, use a defensive pattern like in `datafn/docs/lib/source.ts` (check if it's a function or property before accessing).
